propositions: The _fold_heads function currently merges bundle heads into the worktree HEAD using git merge, making the heal result dependent on the checked-out branch, which causes _require_tracker_on_ref to refuse heals when not on the ref.
The s3 doctor must fold bundle heads into the published ref (refs/heads/<ref>) using git merge-tree instead, so healing succeeds regardless of which branch is checked out.
A dirty tracked worktree on the ref should be refused early before download, but off-branch and detached-HEAD trackers should heal successfully without limitation.
The merge=ours policy for .bridge_state files must be preserved when folding heads, resolving collisions by keeping the tracker's side rather than conflicting.
After off-branch heal, the checked-out branch tip and worktree remain unchanged; after on-branch heal, git status is clean with index and worktree consistent with the moved ref.
All existing refusal tests must convert to successful heal tests, and new coverage must verify merge-policy behavior against the mechanism change from git merge to git merge-tree.
